name: git
description: The distributed version control system: tracks changes, branches, merges, and synchronizes work across machines and teams.

flags.description: Stage changes for the next commit.
Send to / fetch from the remote.

examples.command: git init && git add . && git commit -m "initial commit"
examples.explanation: Starts version control on a project: initialize, stage everything, record.
Downloads a repository with its full history.
The command to run constantly: shows modified files, staged files, and current branch.
Creates and switches to a new branch for isolated work.

examples.output:
a1b2c3d add search feature
e4f5g6h fix sidebar overlap

examples.explanation: Uploads your commits to the remote.

about: Git records snapshots, not diffs: each commit is a full tree referenced by a hash. The staging area (index) lets you compose commits deliberately. Branches are just movable pointers — creating them is instant, which is why feature-branch workflows dominate.
useCases: Version control for any text project.
mistakes: Committing secrets (.env, keys) — they stay in history even after deletion; rewrite history or rotate the secret.
git push --force on shared branches, erasing teammates' work.
warnings: Everything committed is effectively permanent. Review git status and git diff before every commit.
